[USER] The user is looking for a new cherry recipe to try out.  
[PREFERENCE] The user is interested in cherry clafoutis and cherry crisp.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cherry clafoutis is a classic French dessert that serves 6-8 people.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Cherry Clafoutis Recipe:  
- Ingredients: 2 cups fresh or frozen cherries, pitted; 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar; 1/2 cup all-purpose flour; 1/2 teaspoon baking powder; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1/2 cup whole milk; 2 large eggs; 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted; 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.  
- Instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C); whisk together sugar, flour, and baking powder; whisk together milk, eggs, and melted butter; combine wet and dry ingredients; pour batter into baking dish and arrange cherries; bake for 35-40 minutes; dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cherry crisp is a classic American dessert that also serves 6-8 people.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Cherry Crisp Recipe:  
- Ingredients: 2 cups fresh or frozen cherries, pitted; 1/2 cup granulated sugar; 2 tablespoons cornstarch; 1/4 cup all-purpose flour; 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon; 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg; 1/4 teaspoon salt; 1/2 cup rolled oats; 1/2 cup brown sugar; 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces.  
- Instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C); mix cherries, granulated sugar, cornstarch, and flour; transfer to baking dish; mix rolled oats, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt; add cold butter to oat mixture; spread topping over cherry mixture; bake for 40-45 minutes; serve warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.  
[PREFERENCE] The user is interested in trying the cherry clafoutis recipe.  
[USER] The user is considering substituting granulated sugar with brown sugar.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Substituting brown sugar for granulated sugar will affect flavor and texture:  
- Flavor: Brown sugar adds a richer, deeper flavor with notes of caramel and molasses.  
- Texture: The batter may be denser and more moist, resulting in a heavier texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for using brown sugar:  
- Use light brown sugar; reduce to 1 1/4 cups; cover with foil if browning too much.
